title: Azure Container Registry: tasks, geo-replication and scanning

videos.script: Lessons 7, 8 and 9 named an image in a registry called shopregistry. None of them made that registry. This lesson does. {{registry}} Azure Container Registry is a resource in your own subscription, with one address, its login server. It comes in three tiers that share one API. Premium adds the features a business in several regions needs. {{push}} Then a push, taken apart on your laptop. There is no Azure registry here, so an open-source registry stands in. It speaks the same protocol. You will push the shop, read its manifest through the API, and pull it back by digest. {{tag}} Then you will move a tag and watch the old digest stay exactly where it was. That is why a deployment should name a digest. {{tasks}} Next come ACR Tasks: builds that run in Azure, on a commit, on a timer, or when a base image changes. And the two ways of deleting what nobody tagged, one of which ignores the shop's images. {{geo}} Last, geo-replication, one name served from several regions, and scanning by Microsoft Defender, which reads packages and nothing else. Most of the registry is read from Microsoft's documentation. Each section says which part ran.
